title: Collaboration tools
examples: How do I make sure everyone sees the latest changes?
What is the difference between saving and version history?
Can I see who changed something and when?

explain.say: Today we learn about working together on documents online.
Shared documents allow multiple people to edit at once.
Commenting lets you suggest changes without changing the text.
Version history tracks every saved change made to the file.
You can restore the document to any previous version easily.
In a professional setting, these tools save massive amounts of time.

faq.q: What is the main benefit of using shared documents?
faq.a: The main benefit is that everyone works from the single, most current source document. You might also ask: How does shared editing help? Or: Why should I use one file for everyone?
asks: How do I ensure everyone sees the latest changes?
What is the advantage of co-authoring?

faq.q: How do I check who changed what and when?
faq.a: You use the version history feature to see a detailed log of edits. You could also ask: Where is the revision log? Or: Can I see the audit trail?
asks: Where can I see who made the last edit?
How do I track changes in the document?

faq.q: Is commenting the same as editing?
faq.a: No, commenting is for feedback or questions, while editing changes the actual text. Another way to ask this is: Should I use comments or change the text?
asks: What is the difference between suggesting and typing?
Should I use the comment box or rewrite the sentence?

faq.q: What if someone deletes something important?
faq.a: You can restore the document to a previous version before the deletion occurred. This is why version history is so important.
asks: Can I undo a major mistake?
What if someone messes up the file?
How do I get back to an older version?

faq.q: Do I need special software for this?
faq.a: Most modern word processing suites include these features in their online versions. Check the platform you are using for these tools.
asks: Is this only for paid accounts?
Do I need an internet connection?

facts: Shared documents allow simultaneous editing by multiple users.
Commenting is best used for suggestions or questions, not direct changes.
Version history keeps a record of all saved changes over time.
Restoring a version reverts the document to a specific point in the past.

quiz.say: When a team member adds a note asking for clarification, which feature should you use?
quiz.why: Commenting keeps your feedback separate from the main text flow.

wrong.0: Sharing only gives access; it does not create a feedback note.
wrong.2: This changes the document permanently and might confuse the original author.
wrong.3: Version history shows past changes, it is not for making new notes.

quiz.say: If you want to see the document as it looked last Tuesday, which tool do you access?
quiz.why: Version history is specifically designed to track and allow retrieval of past states.

wrong.0: Comments are notes about the text, not records of the entire file state.
wrong.1: The real-time view only shows what is happening right now.
wrong.2: Permissions only control who can access the file, not what the file contained previously.

quiz.say: A colleague changed a key paragraph, but you think the original wording was better. What is the safest first step?
quiz.why: This feature allows you to propose an alternative without overwriting the existing text.

wrong.1: This removes the content without providing a clear reason for removal.
wrong.2: This deletes the colleague's work without them knowing you disagreed.
wrong.3: This is vague; suggesting a specific alternative is more helpful.
